content.thinking:
I'm planning the golem's design in one pass without testing: a hulking 3-meter figure standing at y=0 facing +Z, with a full skeleton of hips, spine, chest, neck, head, jaw, limbs, and fingers, rendered in a basalt-and-gold palette with lava glow accents.

Working out the joint hierarchy now—placing hips, spine, chest, and neck along a slight forward curve, then defining leg joints with thigh/shin lengths and hip/knee/ankle positions, and starting on torso shoulder placement.

Continuing to extend into arms: huge shoulders near 2.75, elbows at 1.95, wrists at 1.15, with oversized fists hovering just above the floor. Then the head and spikes bring total height to roughly 3.7m, and I'm setting up a shared rock-geometry helper for the chunky, flat-shaded body pieces.

I'm defining color palettes for basalt, gold, and glowing lava, plus deterministic jitter and glowing seam rods to place between rock chunks at each limb joint.

I'll add a thinner glowing lava core sweep peeking through gaps between the rock plates for genuine molten seams, confirming glow works on sweep meshes. For gold plates, I'll extrude diamond shapes with a glowing spiral rune texture on a plane placed at the chest, and give the head glowing wedge-cone eyes with a separate rocky jaw built from multiple rock pieces.

Now I'm setting up the imports and helper modules—builder, skeleton joints, rng, paint, texture, toon shading, and glow kit—then starting the build function with the jaw joint and glowing mouth interior details.

Setting up rock and lava color palettes...

Now I'm sketching out the joint hierarchy, starting with a root hip joint oriented upward, and setting up a helper function to define child joints with parent, position, aim direction, and role, while working through typing details for the role parameter.

Continuing to work out spine, chest, neck, and head joint placements and aim directions, using world coordinates rather than local axes to keep the orientation math simpler.

Now I'm sketching the arm joint chain—shoulder, elbow, wrist—with mirrored positions for left and right, and starting to think through how to handle finger joints for each hand.

Each hand gets four fingers plus a thumb, each finger built from two small capsule joints curling slightly forward and down from a central hand point, giving a relaxed, loosely open fist pose.

For the palm I'm placing a chunky icosahedron, then building out the arms with a thicker shoulder-to-elbow capsule and an even bulkier forearm with gold-edged rock details like the reference image. For the legs I'm setting up hip, knee, and ankle joints as a chain, aiming each segment toward the next down to the toe.

I'm deciding to keep toe joints simple and just use rocks for the foot, tallying roughly 36 joints total across hips, spine, arms, and legs. Now I'm writing a helper function to generate each body chunk with its geometry type, color, and placement.

Writing chunk helper code...

Scale uses the icosahedron radius times size for half extents, with random rotation giving tilted rock chunks. For limb armor, I'm sketching a generic function that places n rocks along a bone segment with radial offsets around the axis at interpolated points.

Working through the perpendicular offset vectors and sizing now, planning to elongate rocks along the bone axis by aligning geometry direction with scale applied in local space rather than relying on random rotation.

Writing armor plate helper...

I'm budgeting the part count across body regions, estimating around 400 total plates with icosahedron geometry keeping triangle counts manageable, then planning glowing core elements.

For the lava cores, I'm setting joint balls at bends to show molten material where limbs flex, using glow-strength LAVA coloring. I'm sizing the core radius smaller than the plate radius so the gaps between armor plates naturally expose the glowing interior, rather than drawing separate seam lines.

Switching to torus geometry for the glowing seam bands at joint boundaries, placed along limbs as molten rings. For the torso, I'm thinking a dark lava core capsule from hips to chest with armor plates wrapped around it, scaled larger than the limb plates.

Writing shell generator function...

I'm placing a gold diamond plate behind the chest rune and skipping shell rocks in that region, then sizing the torso and abdomen ellipsoids with glowing capsule cores to shape the chest and pelvis.

I'm sizing the shell plates so they sit on the ellipsoid surface with gaps between them revealing lava glow underneath, checking that the inner plate radius stays roughly at the core's edge even if slightly marginal. For the shoulders I'm building big pauldrons from dark rock clusters topped with a stretched gold spike.

Moving to the head, I'm placing a scaled dark skull ico at the head joint with brow ridge rocks, then starting on the face details.

Now I'm positioning glowing lava-colored eye slits as flattened, rotated icosahedrons jutting slightly from the skull's front, with a bright inner core for extra glow, then adding a crown of dark rock spikes and sweeping gold horns on top before moving to the jaw.

Still placing jaw rocks...

Working out the finger segments with small lava glow spheres at the knuckle joints, naming joints per finger per side, then positioning the wrist, hand, and forearm with bulkier armor blocks spanning elbow to wrist.

Now I'm figuring out the upper arm length from shoulder to elbow, then moving to the legs: hip, knee, and ankle positions with thigh and shin radii, plus foot rock placement using an icosahedron shape sitting flush with the ground.

I'm placing three small toe icosahedrons per foot near the front, sizing and positioning them so they sit just above the ground, then adding a gold toe plate and setting up the ankle bone to aim toward the toes. I'm also considering adding a few small glowing spark particles floating near the shoulders for extra detail.

Now I'm adding dorsal spikes along the back of the chest bone, five dark-gold icosahedrons running upward, plus a glowing vertical lava seam where the shell gaps expose the molten core. I'm also planning gold loincloth plates at the hips using flattened, tilted icosahedrons, along with side diamond accents to match the reference design.

I'm working out a chest rune emblem: a textured plane with a diamond-spiral glyph, backed by a flattened gold diamond plate positioned just in front of the core so it doesn't clip into the shell rocks.

Still writing rune SVG...

I'm also thinking about adding crack-like seams to the rock texture using a cell-based paint function, where cracks near equal-distance cell boundaries get an orange lava tint, letting shading naturally darken them in shadow.

I'll bump paint texture resolution to 2048 for crisp cracks since the painted surface area is sizable. Then I'm picking a mix of icosahedron, dodecahedron, and box geometries for the rock chunk variants.

Still writing helper functions...

For joint balls I'll glow small sphere parts at bone attachments, and for color variation I'm layering two lava tones—a deeper orange LAVA for the core body and a brighter yellow LAVA2 for inner veins, similar to the toon lava-crack look with glowing rings and a thin streak accent.

Now I'm working out the limb-building function, placing armor plates radially around a core cylinder with carefully spaced plate widths and gaps so they don't overlap, repeating this per ring along the limb length with alternating angle offsets for a natural segmented look.

I'm shifting focus to the torso: defining a chest shell with elliptical dimensions, rows of plates, and a skip condition that leaves a bare region on the front for a rune marking based on surface normals. I'm also adding a lower spine/abdomen shell with its own smaller elliptical dimensions.

Below that, I'm roughing out the pelvis and hip shells, noting they'll overlap with the thigh attachment points but deciding that's fine structurally. I'm pairing each torso section with a glowing scaled core sphere (chest, abdomen, pelvis) tied to lava/bone materials, then moving on to start the head with a rock-textured skull block positioned above the neck.

I'm checking whether the eyes actually poke out past the face plate's surface given the skull curvature at that x-position, and realizing the plate may be swallowing the eyes entirely since the plate's front face sits past where the eyes are placed. I need to narrow the face plate so the eyes read as protruding rather than buried inside it.

Still placing crown spikes and horns...

For the gold horns, I'm positioning them angled outward and up from the head, and checking total height stays reasonable for a big golem, roughly 3.8-4m, consistent with towering troll-like lore. Then I'm adding the jaw: a lower bone jaw rock plus a small gold chin spike angled forward and down.

Still fixing teeth and mouth glow placement...

I'm adjusting the skull and jaw positions so they don't overlap -- moving the skull's bottom edge up slightly and the jaw's top edge down -- then placing a small lava-glow slab between them so it peeks out visibly as the mouth's glow, plus defining the jaw joint position.

Now I'm defining the head and neck joints and the small cluster of neck rocks surrounding a glowing core sphere, then moving on to the shoulder pauldron -- stacking several rock shapes of varying sizes and a gold spike to build up the armored look.

Writing spike helper...

Now I'm placing gold diamond details on the hip side plates, extruding outlines oriented along the x-axis for the side normal.

Placing outer thigh diamond plates and rune textures, then moving to knee rock-spike details and finger joint positioning relative to the palm rock bounds.

Now I'm working out the curl path for each finger (base, mid, tip) and placing a separate thumb with its own joint chain on the inner hand side, giving each hand ten joints total. I'm defining the small rock-plate segments along each finger joint, scaling their capsule-like dimensions down toward the tips.

Still placing armor spikes and shields...

I'll skip the back lava vent glow box, and add gold loincloth plates at the front hips using thin ico shapes angled slightly upward, checking they don't clip the pelvis shell. Now I'm starting to define the armor function itself.

Writing armor placement logic...

Working out the TypeScript typing details...

Now I'm designing glowing cores for each limb segment and joint, plus molten cuff rings placed at wrists, ankles, and shoulders using torus geometry, sizing them slightly smaller so they peek out from the plates.

I'm working out the plate counts for each limb segment -- upper arm, forearm, thigh, shin -- with varying radius and plate density, then tallying totals: roughly 48 plates for the arms and 42 for the legs, before moving on to the chest shell's row and plate-per-row layout.

Checking that the paint function correctly uses flat vertex normals so the cel shading renders crisp per-facet colors, and confirming the paint/texture imports and callback signatures are all wired correctly.

Now I'm writing the shell function that distributes scale-like plates across a curved surface in rows, computing angles and positions per row with some randomized jitter...

Writing shell geometry logic...

Adjusting the phi range to ±78 so the top core stays visible through a glowing hole, and adding neck base rocks with randomized color picks from the ROCKS palette, while double-checking the type signatures for the up-direction parameter and bone joint accessor before composing everything together.

Writing joint creation code...

Adding knuckle spikes and back-of-hand geometry, then starting on finger and thumb placement before moving into the leg joint hierarchy with hip and knee attachment points.

Still positioning foot geometry and toes, plus adding a hidden lava glow core inside the foot and checking that it sits just above the ground plane.

Minimum y checks out fine. Now I'm finalizing the file, double-checking unused variables won't trip TypeScript strictness, and adding a dark backing piece behind the eyes for a slit effect before writing everything out.
